correctness.rationale: Genus four and p-rank zero follow from the unique ramification pole order five; the full geometric C3 automorphism group is proved for this exact model in arXiv:2610.13279v1 Lemma 3.3 and its key coefficient equations are reproduced. The included standard-library certificate exhaustively verifies all F_{3^n} affine solutions for n=1..4, independently checks trace-zero counts, and recomputes (7,19,28,91). Weil genus-four reciprocity and Newton identities rigorously give the degree-eight numerator. All v3(c_i)>=i/2 with endpoint (8,4) force the supersingular Newton polygon. Theorem 1.1 excludes lower positive genus with C3 and p-rank zero; genus zero has infinite geometric automorphism group.

originality.rationale: The only genuinely new portion is exact zeta numerator and supersingularity for the published characteristic-three minimal-automorphism genus-four equation, yielding a sharp example asked about in arXiv:2610.13279v1 Question 7.5. Full-text comparison with the same-family standard-form invariant classification (arXiv:2401.08843v2), supersingular genus-four automorphism moduli bounds (arXiv:2405.01282) and explicit prior supersingular Artin–Schreier families (arXiv:0809.0104; arXiv:1410.7031) finds no implication covering this model. Remaining risk of unindexed isomorphic finite-field entries is acknowledged.
residual_risks: An unindexed tabulation of genus-four curves over F3 could contain an isomorphic model and the same zeta numerator.

A supersingular Artin–Schreier existence proof in characteristic three for the full geometric C3 locus might be implicit in literature not identified by the searches; no reviewed stronger theorem was found.

value.rationale: This is the first numerically allowed characteristic-three genus with full geometric deck group and zero p-rank, and the first source explicitly asks which genera can also be supersingular. The exact zeta function supplies a structural Newton-polygon answer, not just another representation of the known automorphism model. The genus-four sharpness is motivated by the source nonexistence thresholds, and the arithmetic certificate makes the answer reusable in further moduli/automorphism studies.
